**Synopsis:**
The NHS experienced its most strained summer on record in England, driven by five heatwaves that pushed A&E attendances, ambulance callouts, and NHS 111 call volumes to all-time highs. The King's Fund and health officials frame this as a structural shift — extreme heat now joins winter as a dual seasonal pressure on the health system. The government announced £1.5bn in NHS investment, though only £32m is earmarked for heat-proofing. The NHS waiting list also rose to 7.3 million in July, putting the government's 2029 treatment target at risk. Climate change is cited as a key driver, with respiratory conditions highlighted as a leading trigger.
